Edge0 

 An open-source streaming MoE inference framework 

 

 Think big. Run here. Sparse. By design. 

 

 macOS · iOS · Android · Linux · Windows One program for every Edge0 model 

 Project 
 
 
 

 Latest release 
 
 
 

 Old release 
 
 
 

 English · 中文 · 日本語 · Español · Français 

 News · About · Models · Quality · Benchmark · Getting started 

 

 News

 

 

 

 
 More updates 

 

 

 
 Full release notes 

- [2026-11-13] We released edge0-145b and edge0-120b , latent mixture-of-experts models derived from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next for a single NVIDIA GPU on Linux or Windows. They run on edge0-strata, which edge0-infer serve and edge0-infer chat start for them; see the model page. Weights on Hugging Face: Edge0-145B-q3k · Edge0-145B-NVFP4 · Edge0-120B-q3k · Edge0-120B-NVFP4 .
- [2026-11-04] We released the unified inference engine edge0-infer : built on GGML, one engine and one native C++ API run the same model on macOS, iOS, Android and Windows, with a CLI, an OpenAI-compatible local server, and chat app examples for desktop, Android and iOS. The first release supports edge0-35b ; edge0-8b follows in a later release. It replaces the Python framework and the per-platform engines; the previous code is kept at tag pre-edge0-infer .
- [2026-09-30] We released the edge0 inference engines for four platforms — iOS, macOS, Android and Windows (source at tag pre-edge0-infer ).
- [2026-09-16] Our technical report is on arXiv: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction.
- [2026-09-08] Initial open-source release of edge0 , together with both model tiers — Edge0-35B-A3B-preview and Edge0-8B-A1B-preview — on Hugging Face and ModelScope.

 

 

 
 Previous release 

→ 35B / 8B release guide — model downloads, architecture, benchmarks, supported platforms and setup instructions.

 

 About

 Edge0 is an open-source streaming MoE inference framework for running large sparse models on consumer hardware. 

Use it through the command line, a local API server, or the Edge0 Chat app.

The latest release brings 145B and 120B latent-MoE models to a single NVIDIA GPU or an Apple Silicon Mac.

Trained natively at 4 bits, both models are available in Q3 K and NVFP4 for local agent workloads.

 edge0-infer provides shared serve and chat commands and selects the engine from the model folder. The latest models run on edge0-strata, a fork of Strata; the previous 35B release runs on the GGML-based native engine.

 Platforms

Support depends on the model and its engine.

 Platform edge0-145b , edge0-120b (edge0-strata) edge0-35b (native engine) 
 --- --- --- 
 Linux NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 13) CPU 
 Windows NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 13) CPU, Vulkan 
 macOS (Apple Silicon) Metal Metal, CPU 
 iOS — Metal 
 Android — CPU 

Use the 145B / 120B setup for the latest release. The previous-release guide covers native backends, platform-specific builds and chat examples. The 8B checkpoint is available; native-engine support is planned.

 Models

 145B / 120B are the current latent-MoE series, derived from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and trained natively at 4 bits. 

They run on edge0-strata through edge0-infer serve and edge0-infer chat , on Linux or Windows with an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA 13, or on macOS with Metal on Apple Silicon.

 145B Q3 K · RTX 5090 D 24 GB: 121.2 tok/s agent decode · 3554.9 tok/s 16K prefill.

 Tier Released checkpoint Inference profile Engine 
 --- --- --- --- 
 edge0-145b Edge0/Edge0-145B-q3k · NVFP4 Q3 K or NVFP4 latent experts (1792), 48 layers, 512 experts, K=10 edge0-strata ✅ (Linux or Windows, NVIDIA GPU; macOS Apple Silicon, Metal, Q3 K) 
 edge0-120b Edge0/Edge0-120B-q3k · NVFP4 Q3 K or NVFP4 latent experts (1280), 48 layers, 512 experts, K=10 edge0-strata ✅ (Linux or Windows, NVIDIA GPU; macOS Apple Silicon, Metal, Q3 K) 

 
 Model overview · 145B Q3 K 

Q3 K · RTX 5090 D 24 GB. Prefill uses a 16K-token input. Quality scores are model-level results.

 

 

 Quality

 145B / 120B

Six benchmarks, six models. Higher is better. Scores are reported by model, not as separate Q3 K and NVFP4 evaluations.

 

Copyable scores and all model names

 
 Copyable scores · all six models 

Bold values indicate the best score in each column.

 Model deepswe 1.1 terminal-bench 2.1 AA-LCR IFBench GPQA-Diamond HLE 
 --- ---: ---: ---: ---: ---: ---: 
 Edge0-145B 64.6 86.5 79.3 80.6 90.4 35.4 
 Edge0-120B 51.3 75.3 81.0 79.3 87.4 31.0 
 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 54.4 82.7 79.7 79.2 90.8 33.8

 Benchmark

 145B / 120B

All throughput figures are in tok/s. The headline uses 145B Q3 K on RTX 5090 D 24 GB.

 
 145B speed table · all machines and builds 

Highlighted rows show Q3 K. Click the table to view it at full size.

 

 
 Copyable 145B speed data 

 Machine Build 4K prefill 16K prefill Chat decode Agent decode 
 --- --- ---: ---: ---: ---: 
 RTX 5090 D 24 GB Q3 K 2169.9 3554.9 99.7 121.2 
 RTX 5090 D 24 GB NVFP4 1839.6 3165.7 79.6 98.3 
 RTX 4090 24 GB Q3 K 2042.0 3179.4 69.9 91.7 
 RTX Spark N1X 60 GiB Q3 K 674.0 770.3 37.7 36.7 
 RTX Spark N1X 60 GiB NVFP4 821.2 922.4 40.1 46.0 
 Apple M2 Ultra (Metal) Q3 K 755.6 800.3 60.9 57.0 
 16 GiB VRAM + 20 GiB RAM Q3 K 249 335 36.8 44.9 

 

 

 
 145B measurement conditions · constrained budget and memory residency 

The 16 GiB VRAM + 20 GiB RAM rows are the same RTX 5090 D 24 GB, not a different card. VRAM is capped with --vram-reserve-mib 8192 ; system RAM by a cgroup ( MemoryMax=20G , no swap). With residency on, the same card holds Q3 K (40.81 GiB of weights)
as 23.14 GiB VRAM + 31.28 GiB RAM, and NVFP4 (47.79 GiB) as 23.25 GiB VRAM + 38.27 GiB RAM — disjoint expert sets,
nothing counted twice.

See Usage & troubleshooting for memory-saving options.

The 16 GiB VRAM + 20 GiB RAM budget is a test limit, not a minimum system requirement. The Apple M2 Ultra row is a Metal measurement.

install.title: Getting Started
install.html:
145B / 120B · edge0-strata

Each model folder (Q3_K or NVFP4, Edge0-145B or Edge0-120B) runs through edge0-infer, from the command line or from the Edge0 Chat desktop app. Keep the folder as it is: edge0-infer identifies the model by model_name in its model.json.

For 145B and 120B, use serve or chat; run belongs to the native engine.

Platform & documentation notes

The build instructions cover NVIDIA GPUs with CUDA 13 on Linux or Windows (x64 or ARM64), and Metal on Apple Silicon macOS.

Build & command-line instructions

1. Build. Clone the repository, then build two parts. Run the launch commands below from edge0-infer/:

git clone https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Edge0.git edge0
  • edge0-strata, the engine: follow "Build (Linux, NVIDIA)", "Build (Windows, NVIDIA)" or "Build (macOS, Apple Silicon)" in edge0-strata/EDGE0.md.
  • edge0-infer: follow "Build" (Linux) or "Windows" in edge0-infer/docs/getting-started.md.

2. Run from the command line. Pass one model folder, such as Edge0-145B-q3k, not the folder that holds several of them. On Windows the program is build\windows\bin\edge0-infer.exe.

build/cpu/bin/edge0-infer serve --model /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k

It prints Listening: http://127.0.0.1:8000 model=<name> once the weights are loaded, where <name> is edge0_145b, and then serves OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints:

curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"edge0_145b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":64}'

edge0-infer chat --model /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k opens an interactive session instead. More options: edge0-infer/docs/edge0-145b.md.

Two GPUs · a second card's expert tier

A second NVIDIA card holds the experts that do not fit in the first one's VRAM, and decoding uses it for both expert formats. The cards need no NVLink or P2P.

edge0-infer runs the engine on one card (its --device is one card), so for two cards start the engine with the config serve/server.py --config reads (it holds exe, args, cwd, env):

  • set "gpu": [0, 1] — the engine's device 0 is the first card, device 1 the second;
  • append to "args": "--peer-device", "1", "--peer-reserve-mib", "1024", "--peer-slots", "0".
cd /path/to/Edge0-145B-q3k
/path/to/edge0-strata/.venv/bin/python /path/to/edge0-strata/serve/server.py \
  --engine strata --config ./model-two-gpus.json

The startup log prints the second card's tier (peer GPU 1: … experts, … GiB), and the server serves the same endpoints as on one card. --peer-device cannot be combined with --layer-split or --expert-cache-device1..3. More: Two GPUs.

Desktop app · Windows · macOS

⬇️ Download: GitHub Releases

Open Edge0 Chat on Windows or macOS (Apple Silicon) and choose a model folder, such as Edge0-145B-q3k, to run the model locally. To build the app from source, follow the Edge0 Chat guide.

Images · vision

mmproj-BF16.gguf in the model folder is the vision encoder. Add this to the model's model.json, next to args:

"vision": {"exe": "/path/to/strata-vision", "mmproj": "./mmproj-BF16.gguf",
           "model": "./model-skeleton.gguf", "gpu": false}

and --vision to "args". strata-vision is not in this repository: setup.py --setup --vision yes fetches it, or build tools/vision in a Strata checkout. The log then says images on; send a picture with /image in the chat, or an image_url part over the OpenAI API.

usage.title: Usage & troubleshooting
usage.html:
145B / 120B · Memory options

Low RAM · SSD offload
  • SSD mode: --mmap-experts — read uncached experts from SSD on demand.
  • Low-memory arguments:
--resident-budget-gib 20 --expert-profile expert-profile.bin

Up to 20 GiB of host RAM for the expert cache; uncached experts are read from SSD on demand. Includes --mmap-experts and disjoint GPU/RAM caches automatically.

Required: a static expert profile. Replace expert-profile.bin with your profile path.

RAM budget · what 20 GiB covers
  • Expert cache: --resident-budget-gib 20 caps host-RAM expert caching at 20 GiB, lowered further to fit available memory.
  • Total RAM: expert cache + other runtime allocations. This flag does not set a total-process RAM limit.
  • Benchmark limit: the 20 GiB total RAM test budget is a separate measurement condition.
GPU / RAM · avoid duplicate experts
  • Enable: --resident-experts or --resident-budget-gib N, with a static --expert-profile.
  • Effect: experts cached in VRAM need no duplicate RAM copy. Compatible with SSD loading.
  • Default: off, prioritizing speed.
  • Automatically enabled: --mmap-experts, --resident-cpu-experts, --resident-pin.
Capacity controls · VRAM and host RAM

These live in the pack's model.json (args for flags, env for environment variables), so a change there applies to every launch of the model.

Flag Meaning Default
--vram-reserve-mib N VRAM left free for the desktop, the driver and other processes; the engine sizes its caches from what remains. 700
--expert-cache N|auto Expert slots kept in VRAM. auto derives the count from the free VRAM after the fixed footprint (projections, MTP draft, verify buffers, D/U device buffers). 0
--kv-resident N KV cells kept in VRAM per QSA layer; the rest streams from pinned host RAM, which frees VRAM for experts. 0
--spec N The MTP drafter's verify window: tokens proposed per check. A bigger window needs bigger verify buffers (about 180 MiB at 4) and pays off when every window has a fixed per-layer cost. Without an MTP layer there is no speculation. 4
--resident-budget-gib N Cap on the host-RAM expert cache. It holds only the experts the VRAM cache does not hold, so the two sets are disjoint, and the value is clamped to the RAM available minus headroom. Needs a static --expert-profile. 0
--mmap-experts Read experts through the pack file on demand instead of pinning them, so nothing is resident in RAM. off
